components.name: Signal Action
components.description: Primary operational action for loading, asking, publishing, or approving.
components.css: .ds-signal-action { min-height: 2.3rem; padding: 0.45rem 0.85rem; border: 1px solid var(--gold); border-radius: 0; background: var(--gold); color: var(--ink); font: 600 0.75rem "IBM Plex Sans", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-signal-action:hover:not(:disabled) { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-signal-action:active:not(:disabled) { filter: brightness(0.96); } .ds-signal-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-signal-action:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: View Edit Mode
components.description: Explicit two-state control that keeps safe viewing distinct from mutation.
components.css: .ds-mode { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; } .ds-mode button { min-width: 3.2rem; padding: 0.45rem 0.65rem; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--muted); font: 500 0.75rem "IBM Plex Sans", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-mode button:hover { background: var(--surface-raised); color: var(--paper); } .ds-mode button.ds-mode-on { background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); } .ds-mode button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Exception Queue Row
components.description: Ranked financial exception with evidence and a direct path into the lake.
components.css: .ds-exception { display: grid; width: 100%; grid-template-columns: 1.8rem 1fr auto; gap: 0.55rem; align-items: center; padding: 0.95rem 0.75rem; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 0; background: var(--surface); color: var(--paper); text-align: left; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-exception:hover { background: var(--surface-raised); } .ds-exception:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-exception-rank { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.65rem; } .ds-exception strong { display: block; font-size: 0.78rem; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-exception small { display: block; margin-top: 0.2rem; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.65rem; } .ds-exception em { color: var(--gold); font-size: 0.76rem; font-style: normal; font-weight: 600; }

narrative.overview:
DoneCornerAI is a near-black operations field where ranked financial exceptions carry more visual authority than generic totals. Signal orange is scarce and operational: it marks the primary exception, active control, agent question, or action that demands attention. Hard hairlines, compact instruments, and dense tabular numbers make the interface feel like a live close-review console rather than a card dashboard.

The system is direct, financially literate, and calm under pressure. It exposes data lineage, agent activity, and irreversible approval as visible working states. The chosen world rejects soft consumer-dashboard decoration and reserves expressive hierarchy for evidence, status, and action.
keyCharacteristics: Exception-first hierarchy instead of equal-weight metric cards.
Near-black flat surfaces separated by tone and hard hairlines.
Signal orange used for priority, active state, and controlled action.
Dense IBM Plex Sans typography with tabular financial numerals.
Square, compact controls with explicit keyboard focus.
Observable agent work and unmistakable human approval.

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Signal orange identifies priority or action; never wash large passive regions with it.

rules.name: The Semantic Channel Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, cyan, danger, and focus colors retain their assigned analytical or state meaning.

rules.name: The Numbers Align Rule
rules.body: Financial values use tabular numerals and right alignment wherever comparison is the task.

rules.name: The Exception Speaks First Rule
rules.body: The primary exception may outrank the page title; routine totals may not.

rules.name: The Operational Density Rule
rules.body: Preserve compact controls and close spatial relationships on desktop; increase target size, not decorative whitespace, on mobile.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Never introduce card shadows, glows, glass effects, or soft elevation; use tone and borders to establish depth.

rules.name: The Hard-Line Rule
rules.body: Structural UI stays square; rounded silhouettes are exceptional and role-specific.

dos: Do lead operational surfaces with ranked exceptions and traceable evidence.
Do separate flat regions with the established tonal sequence and hard hairlines.
Do keep agent status, pending action, and approval controls visible at the moment of consequence.
Do preserve keyboard focus, native dialog focus return, keyboard resizing, and mobile target sizing.
Do keep chart marks and P&L cells directly navigable.
donts: Don't revert the Signal Room to an equal-weight generic card dashboard.
Don't add shadows, glows, glassmorphism, or soft rounded containers.
Don't use signal orange as broad decoration or for passive information.
Don't hide publication approval in a transcript, toast, or collapsed mobile panel.
Don't promote the Close surface's exact signal-strip composition into a universal layout requirement.
